turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, honestly, I didn't even know if coming here would do any good, but I just... I had to talk to someone outside the family because nobody inside the family is listening to me. It’s my husband’s sister. It all comes down to her. For over a year now—well, maybe even a little longer if I really sit down and think about when she first started making those little comments and showing up uninvited—but definitely for a solid year, she has been working this whole family business situation just to get her hands on the money. 

And it’s not just about the money, doctor, it’s about pushing me completely out of the picture. Pushing me out of every single decision that gets made in my own home and my own life. I see what she's doing. She comes around, she acts all sweet and innocent in front of my husband, but I see her pulling him aside, whispering about the accounts and trying to make me look like I don't know what I'm talking about just because I didn't finish high school. And everyone else in the family, they just try to smooth it over, you know? They say, "Oh, you're just stressed," or "She’s just trying to help out." But I am not a fool. No matter how folks try to smooth it over and pretend we're one big happy family, I know exactly what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for more than a year now. She is systematically trying to take control, and I just... I can't get anyone to see the truth of what's happening right under their noses. It's exhausting, it really is, having to watch your back every single day because your own sister-in-law is scheming against you.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unwavering belief that her sister-in-law is scheming to take her money and push her out of the family, maintaining this conviction despite other family members' attempts to provide alternative explanations.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone ever given you clear evidence that your sister-in-law is not doing this, and if so, were you able to accept it?
turns.patient_response:
Clear evidence? Well... see, that’s exactly what my husband tries to say he’s doing. Just the other week—it was a Sunday, I remember because it was right after church and we were sitting at the kitchen table having coffee—he actually went and printed out all these emails and brought home the financial ledgers from the shop. He laid them all out flat on the table, tapping his finger on the paper, saying, "Look, her name isn't on this account," or "Look, she copied you on this message about the new supplier." He really thought that was going to be the end of it. He thought that was his clear evidence that she's just helping out. And my mother-in-law does the exact same thing, always chiming in with how generous she is with her time and how the bank records are perfectly clean. 

But... well, like I just said a minute ago, I know why I'm here. I came because she has been working this family business from the inside to get control of the money and push me out, and a few printed-out emails don't change that. They just don't. Because what my husband doesn't get is that his sister isn't stupid. She’s not going to leave a neat little paper trail of her trying to ruin my life! She does it in the shadows, where he isn't looking. 

So when they show me these ledgers and try to smooth it all over, telling me I have nothing to worry about... no, I can't accept it. I just can't. How could I? I know what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes for over a year now. I see the way she looks at me, I hear the little remarks she makes when my husband walks out of the room to take a phone call, and I see how I'm slowly being boxed out of every single decision. You can't put that in a ledger. So they can wave all the so-called evidence they want in my face, and try to smooth it over so we can just have a nice, quiet, normal Sunday dinner, but I'm the one living it, and I know exactly what she's up to.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes holding a fixed belief that her sister-in-law is plotting against her, and explicitly states she cannot accept concrete contradictory evidence (financial ledgers, emails) presented by her husband.
